svg.title: Detection Starts With Records You Already Hold
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-internal-detection-four-week-build; chapter number: 12; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Detection Starts With Records You Already Hold; subtitle: A four-week build pairing bank-feed testing with a hotline; caption: Hotline-only shops are already behind; Workman Forensics pairs monthly bank-feed tests with tips, and GRF reports hotline usage up 16% over ten years.; assumptions note: The four-week sequencing is an ordering of the cited practitioners' gates; the practitioners did not prescribe a weekly schedule.; note: Sources: Workman Forensics (4CnIVLSoe2o), GRF CPAs & Advisors (bPsS_B4v7Dw), Koegle Law Group (nM5JZ33rgDk), The Brad Weisman Show (Sherry Peel Jackson, _ehHXyRo6fI).; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Export and account check; deliverable: Payroll exports to Excel and owners named on every business bank account; gate: If the payroll provider cannot export, change providers (Workman Forensics).; week: Week 2; title: Bank-feed testing; deliverable: Monthly or quarterly tests and macros running on bank feeds; gate: No hotline-only detection; tips arrive late and the reporter may have been in the scam (Workman Forensics).; week: Week 3; title: Hotline intake; deliverable: Good-faith certification checkbox on every intake report, beyond mail-and-fax intake; gate: Written policy in place before ticking yes on the 990 whistleblower disclosure (GRF CPAs & Advisors).; week: Week 4; title: Investigation and expense scrub; deliverable: Outside investigator assigned; round-number expenses stripped and receipts kept; gate: In-house HR bias screened out (Koegle Law Group); round numbers are the top audit red flag (Jackson).
